cohort: Forty-six women with singleton pregnancy and cephalic presentation diagnosed with placenta previa were included, excluding those with placental abruption, local causes of antepartum haemorrhage, bleeding disorders, or severe medical disorders.
finding: Placenta previa is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, often associated with previous scars and curettage, and frequently managed with obstetrical hysterectomy or caesarean section.
mod_finding: Obstetrical hysterectomy was performed in 65.2% of cases and lower segment caesarean in 34.7%, with the increased caesarean section rate noted as responsible for the increased frequency of abnormally implanted placenta.
